<Rep. Richard E. Neal>: Committee Democrats oppose H.R. 7972, the Taxpayer Workforce Modernization Act. This bill is not a serious modernization strategy for the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). It also does nothing to help taxpayers, efficiently administer the tax laws, lower costs, or address the affordability crisis.
This bill creates a new fellowship program to recruit 10 data scientists from the private sector at salaries of no less than a GS-15 and up to $400,000 (equivalent to the President's salary) to identify complex, new, or emerging tax issues. The data scientists are handpicked by the Commissioner and work at his direction. He also has authority to hire them at the conclusion of their fellowship.
The IRS already has a division dedicated to exactly that work, the Research, Applied Analytics and Statistics (RAAS) Division. The RAAS Division employs data scientists and technical experts who develop advanced tools to detect tax evasion, estimate the tax gap, and strengthen tax compliance. Ten data scientists cannot replace the tens of thousands of IRS employees no longer with the agency. The Trump Administration cut the IRS workforce by 27% (27,600 employees) and that includes a 27% cut to the RAAS Division. If the Majority is serious about hiring data scientists, it should restore full funding to the RAAS Division and hire them through the competitive hiring process.
Furthermore, this bill duplicates existing responsibilities while ignoring the real issue. We are against the pretense that a handful of data scientists can backfill the skilled and dedicated employees fired by the Trump Administration. The IRS has been stripped of its skilled personnel and the funding that it needs to do its job. This is not modernization but demolition.
We should be looking for real ways to help make the IRS more efficient, more effective, and better equipped to serve all taxpayers. Democrats invested $80 billion in the IRS through the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), but Republicans clawed back 90% of that funding. Modernization is an important goal and we support responsible innovation. Thus, we should fully restore the IRS budget, including the IRA investment.
For these reasons, we oppose this bill.
Sincerely,
Richard E. Neal,
Ranking Member.
